concept: Real hardware, on one working bench and its surrounding lab, that visitors can operate.

coordinates.note: Set dimensions and camera positions are authored blockout proposals, not measurements of the real lab or devices. Fit device collections to verified source bounds in Blender.

rules: One room, one scale, one camera; never rescale or relocate a station between beats.
Window direction is fixed in world space. Its screen direction may change as the camera turns.
Time of day changes light intensity and color continuously; the sun must not teleport.
The vehicle and robot remain on the floor throughout the journey.
Keep camera paths outside benches, walls and devices; validate clearances in the animatic.

Drive only during 35–39%; park outside the robot sweep and remain parked in all later views.
During 51–56%, pick the bottle up while stationary, then drive 30 cm while holding it. Do not release it or place it in a box.
Remain on the desk; its screen wakes through the existing demo at the reading rest.
Remain beside the Companion; exact PCB silhouette and LED positions come from KiCad.

export.note: These are future outputs. Real camera matrices and screen quads must come from Blender; no placeholder matrices.

timeline.scroll_definition: 0–100 is scrollY divided by the enhanced stage travel distance of 11 viewport heights; the sticky stage adds one viewport to its document height.
timeline.frame_range_convention: half-open [start, end); adjacent segments share a boundary, not a rendered frame
timeline.duration_note: Reference film time is independent of visit time. Reading rests freeze a pose for their whole scroll interval; there is no automatic scroll or reading timeout.

loader.behavior: Progress follows initial asset readiness. Skip immediately for reduced motion or unavailable media; text and hiring links remain usable. Returning from a project must not replay the loader.

copy.heading: Hardware & firmware.
copy.body: I'm Miguel, an electrical & computer engineer at Carnegie Mellon.
copy.detail: Available for full-time roles after May 2027.

copy.heading: Automated impedance matcher
copy.body: A closed-loop RF matcher that automates manual capacitor tuning.

copy.heading: Real-Time Embedded Vehicle
copy.body: An embedded vehicle with a custom preemptive RTOS, carrier PCB, and PID motor control.

copy.heading: Trash Collection Robot
copy.body: An autonomous bottle-collection robot with computer vision, motor control, and custom power delivery.

copy.heading: Independent builds.
copy.body: Personal projects in embedded systems and circuit design.

projects.heading: Kirby Companion
projects.body: An ESP32-S3 companion with a touch display, Wi-Fi, audio, and a 3D-printed Kirby enclosure.

projects.heading: Kirby LED Keychain
projects.body: A custom LED keychain PCB with a 555 timer driving the light sequence. No microcontroller.

copy.heading: I'm Miguel.
copy.body: I design hardware and write firmware. At Ford, I improved EV power delivery; at Hacker Fab, I deployed automated RF matching. I also teach register-level embedded systems and build my own devices where the enclosure, PCB, and interface have to work together.

career.heading: Hardware Systems Engineering Intern
career.outcome: Resolved a 5.8 V control-unit voltage drop in EV power delivery.

career.heading: Embedded Systems Researcher
career.outcome: Built a $636 RF matcher that holds ~1.2 VSWR at 95–100 W.

career.heading: Head Teaching Assistant
career.outcome: Manage 10 TAs and mentor 60+ students in embedded systems.

smith_motif.geometry: Use real constant-resistance circles and constant-reactance arcs. Center means reflection coefficient Gamma = 0.

uses.meaning: Illustrative loading motif; not a measured convergence trace.
Authored notebook sketch, not documentary lab-note evidence.
Show only what the existing tuner actually computes; map its normalized impedance to Gamma rather than relabeling its current field as a Smith chart.
The same mathematical artwork, recalling the opening.
A visual bookend at center; contact copy does not claim a perfect measured hardware match.

fallbacks.strategy: Ordinary document-ordered sections, authored rest posters and captioned real hardware photos; both personal projects retain their own evidence and project links.
fallbacks.keyboard: Station links land directly on readable rests. Pause camera movement during active demo interaction and keep a visible route to the next section.
fallbacks.theme: Keep the existing light/dark control and accessible solid panel colors; the physical room lighting follows the authored day-to-dusk sequence.
fallbacks.transparency: Solid panels remain readable with reduced transparency or no backdrop-filter.
fallbacks.evidence: Label the room as a rendered presentation. Portrait, employer marks and hardware documentary photos use exact existing files.
